The bullet-riddled body of  Lt Fayaz was found early Wednesday morning in the Herman area of South Kashmir’s Shopian district, police said. I believe that the young and brave military officer, Lt Ummer Fayaz, as well as other Kashmiri security personnel who have been killed are the victims of “takfeer,” a virulent form of jihadism which declares that all those who don’t adhere to the extremist versions of Salafi ideology deserve to be beheaded or brutally killed. reranked_evidence.title: Ummer Fayaz
reranked_evidence.snippet:
Title: Ummer Fayaz
Lieutenant Ummer Fayaz (8 June 1994 – 10 May 2017) was an Indian Army officer from the Kashmir Valley, commissioned into the 2nd Battalion of the Rajputana Rifles shortly before his abduction and execution by militants.[1][2] Born in Sudsona village, Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir, to a farming family, Fayaz attended Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya in Anantnag and later the National Defence Academy, reflecting his aspiration to serve in the military despite regional insurgent pressures.[1][3] Commissioned on 10 December 2016 as a 22-year-old Kashmiri Muslim, his service symbolized integration of locals into national forces amid ongoing militancy.[2][4] On 9 May 2017, while unarmed and on leave attending a relative's wedding in Shopian, he was betrayed by acquaintances and kidnapped by five to six terrorists suspected to be from Hizbul Mujahideen or Lashkar-e-Taiba; his tortured body, bearing multiple bullet wounds, was discovered the next morning in nearby Hermain village.[5][6][7] The incident highlighted targeted killings of Kashmiri personnel in uniform, prompting national outrage and Army vows for justice; in January 2024, Lashkar-e-Taiba operative Bilal Ahmed Bhat, linked to the murder, was eliminated in an encounter.[8][9]. The abduction and murder of Lieutenant Ummer Fayaz on May 9, 2017, involved a module of militants primarily affiliated with Hizbul Mujahideen (HM), a Kashmir-based Islamist insurgent group seeking to establish an Islamic state through armed struggle against Indian control, with supporting elements from Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), a Pakistan-based outfit designated as a terrorist organization by India, the UN, and others for its jihadist operations in Kashmir.[43][44] Jammu and Kashmir Police identified six suspects, including HM commander Adil Hussain Thoker and LeT operative Aqib Ahmad Shah, who participated in the operation using an INSAS rifle stolen from local police.[45][46] The module was led by local HM operative Abbas Ahmad Bhat, previously linked to two other murders, highlighting intra-group coordination typical of hybrid HM-LeT cells in south Kashmir.[47][48] The primary motive was to punish Fayaz as a Kashmiri Muslim perceived as a traitor for enlisting in the Indian Army, thereby serving what militants framed as an occupying force suppressing the Kashmiri independence or Islamist agenda.[49][50] Such targeted killings of local security personnel aim to erode recruitment from the Kashmiri Muslim community—Fayaz being one of few from the Valley in officer ranks—and to signal to civilians the consequences of perceived collaboration, fostering an atmosphere of intimidation amid the ongoing insurgency.[4] HM's chief, Syed Salahuddin, publicly denied group involvement, calling the act "condemnable," though police evidence and subsequent neutralizations contradicted this.[51] Later operations eliminated key perpetrators, including LeT's Bilal Ahmed Bhat in January 2024, confirming the groups' roles in the premeditated attack timed during Fayaz's attendance at a family wedding in Kulgam.[9][14].
